original_card.question: Can a decoder deliver the local paid mass in fewer, larger-rank children (block frame climbs instead of rank-1 to rank-3 steps)?
methods: Find one exact small decoding identity whose frame path climbs in blocks, and price its complete per-call profile.
Bound the best effective child rank achievable for one fixed support alphabet, including copies, frames and restoration.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A per-call local profile, with all copied information, frames and restoration counted, whose ceiling exceeds the selected word's by at least 5%; masked or overcomplete supports must change an assumption of the eight-term all-pairs bound.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected word's per-call local profile, its packing ceiling and the lever table; run levers.py for the ideal budget of the lever you target.
first_step.scope: Positive control and planning budget only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Before any synthesis, write the candidate per-call local profile (and centre charge / unpaid coordinates if changed) and screen it with ceiling.ceiling(); reject it if even the ideal ceiling does not beat the selected word's by your stated margin. Ideal budget: rank-16 delivery is 2.31x (levers.py).
original_card.bottleneck_link: Rank-1 children are about half of recursive cost; the selected word's effective child rank is about 3.9. Larger-rank delivery lowers recursive cost per unit of paid mass.
allowed_variations: One masked, overcomplete or block decoder family with exact labels and supports.
A scoped lower bound on effective rank for one alphabet.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Repacking idle remainders of an unchanged word (covered by the packing ceiling).
Repeating the eight-term all-pairs search inside its proved scope.

actual_scope: Audit of one implication in open PR1779 (1337isnot1337, head 1e3128bf): its 8-batch maximum counts only contiguous runs of rank-1 climbs in the selected gauge44 provider. Count disjoint 16-batches of rank-1 climbs on distinct destinations when a rank-1 climb may move, inside its phase, past events that do not touch its register; check the reordered programs with the retained independent local checker; price the counts with ceiling.ceiling() under PR1779's zero-charge, mass-preserving convention.
scope_change_reason: PR1605/discussion 1596 already price rank-shape budgets; PR1779 presents the source chronology as bounding the diagonal-batch subfamily below the card's 5% gate. Whether that bound is a property of the provider or of the contiguity rule decides whether this route is closed.
bottleneck_link: Rank-1 children are about half of the complex recursive cost; this decides whether the selected provider's chronology itself blocks rank-16 batching (it does not: 134 legal batches, +39.5% zero-charge ceiling), moving the question to the waived gathering/restoration charge.
stop_rule: Stop at a certified legal batch count with checker replay and exact ceilings; do not construct a physical diagonal rank-16 child or price its gathering.
evidence: verify.py: archive and member pins; batch.py reorder (non-rank-1 event order unchanged, same multiset) gives 134 batches per orientation, per-phase cap 149; retained hpe_audit_local.py accepts the reordered programs with a receipt equal to the original's (and the original's equals the pinned selected receipt); two mutation controls rejected; PR1779's contiguous rule re-implemented counts 8 -> 134; exact ceilings: 22 batches miss the +5% gate, 23 pass, 134 give a_hi 0.002358018698467.

open_questions.question: What per-batch gathering/restoration charge can 134 diagonal rank-16 batches afford while still passing the +5% gate (and other targets)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: With the chronology no longer binding, the waived charge is what decides the diagonal-batch route.
open_questions.first_step: Specify the contract for 16 registers at different frames a_i -> b_i and price it against the sharp idle-displacing headroom (1,258 extra rank-1 children per call at 134 batches, verify.py).
open_questions.blocked_by: The physical contract of a diagonal rank-16 child over registers at different frames is not specified (inherited unexamined from PR1779).

open_questions.question: Charge headroom under PR1605's on-top convention (overhead added on top of the idle bill).
open_questions.why_it_matters: The idle-displacing headroom is an accounting upper bracket; the on-top one is the conservative bracket.
open_questions.first_step: Add the overhead moment term outside ceiling()'s local-profile interface and bisect.
open_questions.blocked_by: ceiling() only takes a local profile; needs a small extension.
